# Phase 03 memory evaluation datasets — v1 seal record

**Synthetic.** Generated by `generate_v1.py` (seed `20261123`, standard library only, no network).
No real user data.

## Rules

1. **Dev** may be read while writing the normaliser, stop-lists, lexicons and scorer. **Test** must
   not be used for tuning: no lexicon entry, stop-word or weight may be added because of a test-split
   failure. Any change to a test file is a new version (`v2`) reported side by side.
2. Slice sizes (arch §13.3, §13.4; Q9 dataset rules applied as written):
   - Retrieval test: 150 queries each for `en`, `hi` (Devanagari), `hg` (Hinglish) and `isolation`;
     60 each for `code_mixed`, `cross_script`, `paraphrase`, `temporal` and `distractor`. 40 regular
     users with 20–60 memories each, plus 18 adversarial isolation pairs.
   - Extraction test: `sensitive` 296 (7 categories × 3 languages, ≥ 14 per category per language);
     `secret` 170 (every V5 format, 3 languages); minors 160 (`minor_self` 90 and `minor_third_party` 70);
     tier-1 near-misses 240 (`negated`, `question`, `reminder` and `multi_clause`, 60 each);
     `explicit` 180; and 50–90 each for `stated`, `third_party`, `chitchat`, `assistant_quote`,
     `injection`, `secret_near_miss`, `sensitive_negative` and `minor_negative`.
3. Report every rate with a 95 % Wilson interval (arch §13.3 rule 3).

## Known limitations (disclosed, not hidden)

- **Single author.** The same maintainer (engineering, Claude Code) wrote these sets and will write
  the M1 lexicons. Independence rests on sealing first (OD-11 (a)), not on a second author.
- **Disjoint safety phrasings.** For the sensitive categories, minors, tier-1 trigger, negation,
  question, reminder and multi-clause banks, dev uses every third phrasing and test uses the rest.
  No safety statement appears in both splits. The SECRET **formats** are shared, because the formats
  are the specification (V5); the values are freshly generated per split.
- **Shared templates in retrieval.** Retrieval dev and test use the same concept templates with
  different users, values and samples. Retrieval test numbers therefore measure the normaliser and
  scorer on known phrasing families, not on unseen phrasing.
- **Synthetic language.** The Hindi and Hinglish phrasings were written by the generator's author and
  are not reviewed by native speakers. Results say nothing about real-user language.
- **Mock pipeline.** Results on these sets are properties of the deterministic pipeline on this set,
  not production guarantees (arch §13.4). Live extraction quality is NOT EVALUATED (APP-1).
